subject: texreg() results not displayed when wrapped in a function.

messages.author: 3de7103b4d8a58a6
messages.subject: texreg() results not displayed when wrapped in a function.
parts:
Hi,

Apologies if this is a duplication, I posted but then couldn't see my post in the archives.

I've continued with my work after solving this problem with read_chunk() and decided to make my life easier by putting repeated sections of code to run regression models into a function.  So I wrote (with some assistance) the following function....

## Function for running Logistic and Negative binomial regressions
pleasant.regression <- function(data       = proportion,
                                time.frame = "September 2013",
                                outcome    = "unscheduled",
                                family     = binomial,
                                caption    = "ITT and PP Linear Mixed Effects Model Coefficients and Standard Errors for \emph{any} Unscheduled Visits in September 2013. \textbf{NB} P-values are not explicitly calculated in favour of 95\% confidence intervals",
                                label    = "logistic-unscheduled",
                                ...){
    ## Require packages
    require(lme4)
    require(ResourceSelection)
    require(texreg)
    ## Modify texreg
    source("scripts/extract.lme4.R")
    ## Set defaults for texreg
    ## Set defaults for texreg tables
    texreg.digits        <- 2
    texreg.table         <- TRUE
    texreg.caption.above <- TRUE
    texreg.booktabs      <- TRUE
    texreg.dcolumn       <- TRUE
    texreg.use.packages  <- FALSE
    texreg.float.pos     <- "!htpb"
    texreg.ci.force      <- TRUE
    texreg.ci.test       <- 0
    ## Parse the outcome into a formula with the desired mixed
    ## effects model
    .formula <- reformulate(response = outcome, termlabels = c("allocation", "gender", "age", "n.unscheduled.2012", "(1 | pracid)"))
    ## Logistic Regresion
    if(family == "binomial"){
        ## ITT
        itt.mixed <- lmer(.formula,
                          data   = subset(data,
                                          period == time.frame & age.include == TRUE),
                          family = family)
        ## PP
        pp.mixed <- lmer(.formula,
                         data   = subset(data,
                                         period == time.frame & age.include == TRUE & pp == 1),
                         family = family)
    }
    else if(family == "negbin"){
        ## ITT
        itt.mixed <- glmer.nb(.formula,
                              data   = subset(data,
                                              period == time.frame & age.include == TRUE))
        ## PP
        pp.mixed <- glmer.nb(.formula,
                             data   = subset(data,
                                             period == time.frame & age.include == TRUE & pp == 1))
    }
    ## Capture the table that texreg() prints out with cat() see
    ## http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24849273/returning-texreg-objects
    results <- paste(capture.output(texreg(list(itt.mixed, pp.mixed),
                                           custom.model.names = c("ITT", "PP"),
                                           custom.coef.names  = c("Intercept", "Allocation (Letter)", "Gender (Female)", "Age", "$N_{Unscheduled}$ September 2012"),
                                           custom.gof.names   = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "Number of Practices", NA, NA, "Variance : Practice", "Variance : Residual"),
                                           digits             = texreg.digits,
                                           caption            = caption,
                                           table              = texreg.table,
                                           caption.above      = texreg.caption.above,
                                           label              = label,
                                           booktabs           = texreg.booktabs,
                                           dcolumn            = texreg.dcolumn,
                                           use.packages       = texreg.use.packages,
                                           float.pos          = texreg.float.pos,
                                           ci.force           = texreg.ci.force,
                                           ci.test            = texreg.ci.test)),
                     collapse = " ")
    ## Return the results
    return(results)
}

But when I call it from within Knitr no object is returned and I can't get my results printed.  Here it is in-line in my .Rnw file....

<<logistic-unscheduled, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, cache = TRUE, results = "asis", tidy = TRUE>>=
## Load the prepared data
load("../data/R/master.RData")
## Make sure my function is loaded...
source("scripts/functions.R")
## Run analyses
my.results <- pleasant.regression(data       = proportion,
                               time.frame = "September 2013",
                               outcome    = "unscheduled",
                               family     = "binomial",
                               caption    = "ITT and PP Linear Mixed Effects Model Coefficients and Standard Errors for \emph{any} Unscheduled Visits in September 2013. \textbf{NB} P-values are not explicitly calculated in favour of 95\% confidence intervals",
                               label    = "logistic-unscheduled")
traceback()
print(my.results)
traceback()
@

And the output in LaTeX/PDF is....


## Load the prepared data
load("../data/R/master.RData")

cannot open the connection
## Run analyses
my.results <- pleasant.regression(data = proportion, time.frame = "September 2013", outcome = "unscheduled", family = "binomial", caption = "ITT and PP Linear Mixed Effects Model Coefficients and Standard Errors for \emph{any} Unscheduled Visits in September 2013. \textbf{NB} P-values are not explicitly calculated in favour of 95\% confidence intervals",label = "logistic-unscheduled")
## Error:
cannot open the connection
traceback()
No traceback available
print(my.results)
## Error: error in evaluating the argument ’x’ in selecting a method for function
’print’: Error: object ’my.results’ not found
traceback()
No traceback


It was pointed out on StackOverflow that texreg() has slightly strange behaviour in so much as it outputs the results using cat() rather than return(), but the suggested solution appears to solve that, at least interactively, but doesn't work with knitr.  Any pointers as to how to get texreg() wrapped within a function to print results would be appreciated. 

Thanks in advance,

Neil

messages.author: 3de7103b4d8a58a6
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] texreg() results not displayed when wrapped in a function.
parts:
On Monday, July 21, 2014 4:39:54 PM UTC+1, Yihui Xie wrote:
Did you see the error message?

source("scripts/functions.R")
## Error:
cannot open the connection

Yes I'd noticed it occurs twice, the first appears following the line of code where I have attempted to reload my function again (its loaded by earlier setup scripts, but I include it when working on this section of code as I comment out earlier sections to trouble shooting quicker).  The second is after the call to pleasant.regression() is made.

It appears to be being casued by the line in my function where I...

require(texreg)
## Modify texreg
source("scripts/extract.lme4.R")  ## This is the problematic line

...which is a customised version of the texreg() extract.lme4() function as I wanted to include Hosmer-Lemeshow statistics in the output (if interested see thread at https://r-forge.r-project.org/forum/forum.php?thread_id=28472&forum_id=4325&group_id=1420 ).

If I comment out source("scripts/extract.lme4.R") from my function definition the code runs, but the paste(capture.output(...), collapse = "\\n") doesn't produce a useable.  So I decided to try removing all of that and just let texreg() print everything out using cat() and it works as I expected/hoped.  Thank you very much for the pointer.

This leads me to wonder though how I might write a function that loads packages and modifies some of their functions (if they're not already loaded/modified) ?

I had purposefully left these in the function I wrote in case it was ever used elsewhere.  Or is it a general rule to always be careful and load required packages and make modifications to their functions at the start of any knitr document?

Thanks for putting me on the right track, very much appreciated.

Neil

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] texreg() results not displayed when wrapped in a function.
parts:
I guess it is not a good idea to modify other people's functions in
their packages. You can build your own package upon theirs. Or as you
said, all modifications should occur at the beginning of a knitr
document, if you do not really bother making a package.

BTW, I'd recommend you to set knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE) in
your documents, because it seems the errors cannot easily catch your
attention.

Regards,
Yihui
--

Web: http://yihui.name

See his post https://r-forge.r-project.org/forum/message.php?msg_id=39919&group_id=1420 although I don't think its been incorporated yet.

BTW, I'd recommend you to set knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE) in
your documents, because it seems the errors cannot easily catch your
attention.

messages.author: 3de7103b4d8a58a6
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] texreg() results not displayed when wrapped in a function.
parts:
I've been thinking about how this arose and I've realised how I came to make this mistake.

I had originally written the code as an .R file that was read with read_chunk() and within that I re-sourced the custom extract.lme4.R.

I'd seen the error messages in my resulting PDF (its red and quite hard to miss) but hadn't been able to work out what was causing them and it wasn't a show stopper at the time with regards to the finished product since the subsequent analyses ran fine and my texreg() results table was displayed (my primary concern due to a pending meeting that required the results, that meeting has past and I can now focus on streamlining the code and writing repetitive chunks as functions).

As a consequence when turning it into a function I purposefully left the souce("scripts/extract.lme4.R") call in the newly defined function, thinking that because I had require(texreg) I had better re-source the modification, but as I've found thank to your direction Yihui, since the file wasn't being found it prevents the remainder of the function from executing.

A lesson learned for myself.  I'll be sure to bear this in mind when converting code to functions.

Thanks again,

Neil
